classification.difficultyReason: The task is a standard age word problem: set up two linear equations, substitute and solve. Parts a and b are the same demand as p48-q20 (34). Part c, the hardest, requires reading 'twice the age her son was 4 years ago' as mixed time shifts, with +4 on one side and -4 on the other. That is a small extra translation step. The solving is easy, with integer answers and no fractional ratio, so it sits near p50-q27 (39) and below the simultaneous-equation rectangle problems (p46-q15).

content.prompt: Sophie is 24 years older than her son. Find Sophie’s current age if:

children.label: a
children.prompt: in 4 years’ time, she will be twice her son’s age.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x+4&=2(y+4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+28&=2y+8\\y&=20\\x&=44\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 44 years old.

children.label: b
children.prompt: 4 years ago, she was twice her son’s age.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x-4&=2(y-4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+20&=2y-8\\y&=28\\x&=52\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 52 years old.

children.label: c
children.prompt: in 4 years’ time, she will be twice the age her son was 4 years ago.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x+4&=2(y-4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+28&=2y-8\\y&=36\\x&=60\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 60 years old.
